mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of episodes where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in at least 70% of instances where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero during periods when UNRATE exceeds 5.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces input demand and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where INDPRO declines for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual monetary tightening and inflationary pressure, which increases real discount rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and consumer confidence, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST exceeds 12-month moving average for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods when HOUST is above its 12-month moving average for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) within the same month indicates a statistical anomaly or data inconsistency, which historically coincides with subsequent market volatility and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises while UNRATE rises in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of months where PAYEMS and UNRATE both rise.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year decline in Real Personal Income (proxied by RSAFS) exceeding 1% for six consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in household purchasing power, which reduces demand for goods and services and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS YoY change < -1% for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of episodes where RSAFS falls by more than 1% year-over-year for six consecutive months.
